title: Real per-run cost measurement for Mode 3 (token×price+cache, wall-clock, variance) — augments static line-count
problem: Mode 3 cost-engineering measures only static prompt line-count (context_load via wc -l) as a token proxy. It is blind to actual per-run dollar cost, cache economics, wall-clock duration, and cross-run variance. On 2026-06-14 — a visibly heavy operator session (12-PROP OBE audit, PROP-100/096-C1/098 implementation) — tinker's 08-41 Mode 3 run wrote proposals_written:[] and called the pipeline clean, because the instrument cannot see that decider/analyst/curmudgeon runs cost real money that an optimization could reduce. The standing candidates (decider dispatcher-split 4153L; workspace-sync script-extraction 1585L) have been carried unactioned for weeks because line-count alone provides no $-saving signal to justify the design work.

q1_access_path_probe.question: Can a tinker scheduled run read JSONL transcripts for other scheduled agents (or its own past runs)?
q1_access_path_probe.method: From this live tinker run (session gracious-eager-clarke), probed /sessions/ ownership and attempted cross-session reads.
findings: Each scheduled run is its OWN session. Its transcript lives at /sessions/<that-session>/mnt/.claude/projects/<proj>/<run-uuid>.jsonl.

Other sessions' mnt/ dirs are mode 750 owned by nobody:nogroup. Tinker runs as uid 5495 (gracious-eager-clarke) and gets 'Permission denied' on every other session's mnt/. Hypothesis (b) from the directive is CONFIRMED: per-session isolation, no shared mount.

Across ALL of /sessions/, exactly ONE *.jsonl is findable+readable: tinker's OWN current run. Tinker cannot read other agents' transcripts AND cannot read its own PAST runs (those live under now-locked prior session IDs).

The current live transcript IS fully parseable: usage.{input_tokens,output_tokens,cache_creation_input_tokens,cache_read_input_tokens} present on every assistant message; nested usage.cache_creation.ephemeral_{5m,1h}_input_tokens present and correctly distinguishes 5m vs 1h cache writes; usage.model present (claude-opus-4-8).
q1_access_path_probe.conclusion: JSONL-scraping by tinker is a dead end for cross-agent/cross-run cost history (permission boundary + per-run session ephemerality). Per the directive's own constraint, the fix is AGENT-SIDE SELF-REPORT, not a cross-session access hack. Each agent CAN read its own live transcript (own uid) at end of run and write usage+cost into its existing report-*.json, which git-propagates and is readable by tinker cross-agent.
q1_access_path_probe.consequence_for_phasing: This collapses the directive's imagined Phase 1 ('tinker computes from currently-available data') down to 'tinker measures its OWN run' — because that is literally the only transcript tinker can read. The durable cross-agent data source IS the self-report mechanism the directive labelled Phase 2. To honor the 'do not change every agent prompt in Phase 1' constraint, Phase 1 here changes ONLY tinker's own prompt (allowed — it is tinker's own surface); Phase 2 rolls the identical block to the other 11 agents.

q3_pricing.note: inference_geo/fast-mode/batch modifiers NOT applied (pipeline uses global standard rates).
q3_pricing.cache_multipliers: 5m write 1.25x base, 1h write 2x base, cache read 0.1x base
q3_pricing.helper: monitor/scripts/compute-run-cost.js (delivered with this PROP). Prices every column incl. nested 5m/1h cache-write split; flat cache_creation_input_tokens (no nested split) priced as 5m (conservative-low). CLI: <transcript.jsonl> | --dir <d> | --json <usage> --model <id>.

q2_wallclock.recommended: Option (a) — compute duration from the agent's own transcript first/last message timestamps (transcript_duration_sec in the helper). Zero extra prompt logic beyond the self-report block; the agent already reads its transcript to extract usage.
q2_wallclock.alternative: Option (c) — PRELUDE RUN_STARTED_AT marker. More precise (captures pre-first-LLM-call setup) but needs a second prompt edit. Adopt only if (a)'s transcript-span proves materially short of true wall-clock.

q4_variance.design: Once Phase 2 self-report data accumulates in git (each agent's report-*.json carries cost_usd+tokens+duration), tinker Mode 3 reads the trailing-14d report-*.json per agent and computes median, p95, max cost-per-run and duration-per-run.
q4_variance.alert: Flag any agent where p95 cost > 3x median cost (signature of unbounded loops / rare-mode walks). Example today: a tinker Mode 3 deep-walk vs a Mode 0 no-op would differ visibly; the instrument should make that legible.

q5_composite.metric: daily_cost = median_cost_per_run x runs_per_day x substantive_rate (1 - no_op_rate). Rank agents by daily_cost; surface top-3.
q5_composite.rationale: Optimization targets are agents that run often AND cost much per run AND mostly do real work. Cheap, rare, or mostly-no-op agents are not targets even if individually pricey.
q5_composite.expected_top_target: Almost certainly decider (Opus, 3 slots/day, largest static load 4153L) — but the new instrument is precisely what is needed to CONFIRM this rather than assume it. PROP-021 (curmudgeon dispatcher optimization, drafted >1y ago, never integrated, claims 46K->2K tokens/run) should be re-surfaced as a candidate IF cost data confirms the savings claim.

q6_linecount_coexistence.decision: KEEP the existing context_load static-line-count section unchanged. It catches PROMPT DRIFT (an agent's prompt grew 50 lines without authorization) — a different failure mode that per-run token measurement does NOT catch. Both sections coexist in the report. This PROP AUGMENTS, never replaces.

q7_phase2_operator_session.note: Operator-Claude session cost (today's OBE audit, PROP-100 author+implement) is the BIGGER blind spot but is OUT OF SCOPE here. It would require operator-session JSONL aggregation, which raises privacy/scope questions out of band. Deferred to a future PROP (call it Phase 3) only if the agent-side instrumentation lands cleanly.

q8_action_threshold.formula: Rank agents by measured daily_cost (Q5). The #1 agent — IF it has no optimization PROP INTEGRATED in the trailing 30d targeting its dominant cost component — gets an optimization PROP authored THIS run. Numeric gate: daily_cost > $20/day to qualify at all (below that the design cost of an optimization PROP exceeds plausible savings).
q8_action_threshold.honest_calibration_caveat: The directive asks this be calibrated so TODAY triggers exactly one action. That is not yet possible: Phase 1 can measure ONLY tinker's own cost (Q1 permission boundary), so there is no cross-agent ranking to apply the gate to. Therefore Phase 1's single committed action is to MAKE THE DATA EXIST (ship the helper + tinker self-report; Phase 2 rolls it out). The threshold goes live after >=7d of Phase-2 data. First-fire prediction: decider — UNLESS PROP-095 (decider runtime wrappers, integrated 2026-06-13) already moved decider's cost enough to drop it below the gate, which the new instrument will, for the first time, be able to verify rather than guess.
q8_action_threshold.anti_indefinite_list: This formula is a commitment: when daily_cost says agent X is top and un-optimized, tinker authors the PROP that run — it does not re-add X to a standing list. That is the behavioral change from today's state.

validation_run.description: Q-deliverable item 7. Directive asked for tinker's last-7-days cost; Q1 proves last-7-days is inaccessible (past runs locked), so validation is tinker's CURRENT live run — the only readable transcript.
validation_run.note: Per-message usage sums to true billed cost because each API turn is billed independently and cache_read is charged on every turn (not deduplicated across turns).
validation_run.headline: This partial Opus run = ~$8.57, of which ~$7.56 (88%) is cache write+read. Confirms the directive's core assertion: a cost model that ignores cache columns is wrong by ~5x. 1h cache writes (511K tok @ $10/MTok = $5.11) dominate even cache_read ($2.45).

phasing.phase_1: tinker-side ONLY (no other agent prompt changes — honors constraint). (a) commit monitor/scripts/compute-run-cost.js [done with this PROP]; (b) add a ~6-line end-of-run block to tinker.md that runs the helper on tinker's own transcript and writes a self_cost{model,tokens,cost_usd,duration_sec} object into report-*.json; (c) Mode 3 reads accumulated tinker self_cost rows from git report history to build tinker's own cost time-series. context_load (line-count) untouched.
phasing.phase_2: Roll the identical self-report block to the other 11 agents (decider, analyst, analyst-baby, curmudgeon, curmudgeon-verify, integrity, social, poller, workspace-sync, dome-mirror, prune-integrity). Each writes usage+cost_usd+duration to its own report-*.json. Then tinker Mode 3 aggregates cross-agent, computes Q4 variance + Q5 composite, applies Q8 threshold. Phase 2 is its own PROP authored after Phase 1 proves the block works.
phasing.phase_3_optional: Q7 operator-session cost. Privacy/scope review required. Only if Phases 1-2 land cleanly.

constraints_honored: Q1 found no cross-agent JSONL access -> recommended fix is agent self-report, NOT a cross-session access hack.
context_load static line-count NOT deleted or weakened (Q6).
Phase 1 does not change every agent's prompt (only tinker's own).
Measurement is actionable: Q8 commits tinker to author an optimization PROP when daily_cost ranks an un-optimized agent #1.
Cache-read AND cache-write (5m vs 1h) priced correctly; validation shows cache is 88% of cost — ignoring it would understate by ~5x.
obe_closure_note: Phase 1 + Phase 2 both shipped 2026-06-14 (commits 3ba3c39 + b054e5d): monitor/scripts/{compute-run-cost.js,write-self-cost.sh} + self_cost block added to 11 agent prompts (tinker via merge into report-*.json; analyst+curmudgeon+decider+analyst-baby+curmudgeon-verify+integrity+poller+social+dome-mirror+workspace-sync via append to cost-history.jsonl). 10 new git-append-only JSONL files registered in build.js + workspace-sync.md + CLAUDE.md. Empirical validation: tinker self_cost $8.11/run, curmudgeon $10.03/run, both ~85% cache. Phase 3 (operator-session cost) deferred per PROP-101 — privacy/scope review required.
